idea: Riso is the print shop: three fluorescent inks laid one pass at a time over a navy key plate, each slipped by a hair, on uncoated paper with a grain you can feel. Headlines overprint themselves. Pages go full-bleed in one ink. Tags hang off things. It makes any subject feel like a picture book someone made by hand, and it is at its best when the story moves in chapters.
use_for: Scrolly stories and picture-book explainers, chaptered long reads, posters and zines, launch pages that want warmth with a spine.
avoid_when: Dense dashboards (three inks and a key cannot carry twelve series), institutional or legal subjects, anything that must look neutral, or long UI-heavy apps.
principles_headline: Three inks. One key. Everything slips a little.
principles: Blue, pink and yellow over navy. There is no fourth ink; a new colour is a new plate, and you do not have one.
Inks multiply where they cross. Gradients and blur do not exist in a riso; the halftone dot does.
A headline is printed three times, each pass off by a hair. The slip is the signature; keep it under .05em.
Chapters open full-bleed in one ink with the number enormous. Cards are sheets with a hard shadow, slightly turned.
Facts live on luggage tags and folios: mono caps, a punched hole, a string. The reader picks them up.
voice: Storybook present tense: "On a Tuesday a crate arrives."
Chapter numbers in roman, folios in mono: "Chapter II · p. 6".
Short sentences, concrete nouns, one italic aside per page.
Name what is invented: "fictional batch · figures illustrative" in the imprint.
colour_headline: Paper, key, and three inks that multiply.
colour_note: Paper first. Night is the ink page: the key plate becomes the ground, type goes paper, and the fluorescent inks stay fluorescent. Yellow is never text and never a line; it is a ground and a highlighter. Blue is the working ink: actions, the first series, headline colour. Pink is the slipped plate and the badge. Status colours exist for callouts and tags only and always come with a word.
chart_note: The three inks in print order, then the key at half strength, then green. Bars overprint (multiply) where they stack; lines are the key plate at 2px.
type_headline: Fraunces at full soft and wonk; Space Mono for everything printed small.
type_note: One serif does the whole page: Fraunces at 900 with SOFT 100 and WONK 1 for display (the wonky a and g are the point), at 500 for reading, at 500 italic for decks. Space Mono carries labels, folios, tag facts and figures. No sans anywhere.
space_headline: A 9px dot pitch, a 2px key edge, a 6px slip.
space: Gaps between cards so hard shadows never touch.
Chapter page padding on wide screens.
edges: Everything. A riso has no rounded corners except the punched hole in a tag.
Cards, buttons, fields, tables, the ticker band. Hairlines are for table rows only.
Contents lists and ledgers use a dashed key rule between items.
Cards and tags sit a fraction off square, alternating sign down the page.
depth: 6px 6px 0 key on cards and buttons; pink at night.
9px 9px 0 key on step cards and tags.
A 9px dot screen in one ink, masked to a corner, stands in for any gradient.
A fractal-noise grain at 40% multiply on covers and chapter pages. Never on UI.
motion: Cards lift 4px and straighten to 0°, 160ms. Buttons move into their shadow on press.
Step cards use the kit reveal-up; chapter words are printed in one pass, never faded.
A figure may print plate by plate: three clip-path wipes, 1.2s each, blue then pink then yellow. Once per page.
The yellow ticker uses animate-marquee at 38s. One per page, and it carries facts, not decoration.
Stamps and badges arrive with a spring: scale .6 to 1 at cubic-bezier(.2,1.6,.4,1).
Everything printed, nothing moves. Every state is visible without it.
components_headline: The kit prints on paper; the key edge and the slip are classes.
components_note: Kit components take Riso through the contract: paper and sheet grounds, blue primary, yellow secondary, pink ring, zero radius. The 2px key edge, the hard shadow and the turn are classes on authored elements: ri-card, ri-btn, ri-tag.

stats_note: A door: the number printed big on one ink block with a halftone shadow, the label beside it. Three doors, three inks. Figures come from data.
callouts:
Figures illustrativeThe batch is fictional; the arithmetic is real.
NoteBlue means the working ink. A fact about the batch, not an alarm.
DonePrinted. All three plates landed.

callouts_note: A callout is a sheet with a dashed key rule and a folio in the corner. Status is the ground tint and the folio word; the text stays key.
chart_comp_note: Charts take the inks in print order: blue, pink, yellow. Stacked bars overprint; no gradients; labels in mono.
table_note: Tables are key on sheet with hairline rows, mono figures, and the 2px edge on the container.
card:
p. 6

Dot, who was dropped

Screen cracked corner to corner, everything else fine. Twenty minutes, one new screen, and Dot goes back through door one.
card_note: A step card: a sheet with the key edge, a 9px slip, a folio tab and a fraction of a turn. Highlights are a yellow bar behind the words, never a colour change.

hand.headline: Three plates, printed one after another.
hand.note: Riso draws any subject as a print: the fills go down first as colour plates (blue, pink), offset by 4px and multiplied where they cross, then the key plate draws every edge in 2px navy. No gradient, no blur, no rounded strokes; dots stand in for tone. The subject changes; the press does not.
rules: 2px navy, round caps. Every edge, drawn last, slightly off the fill.
Flat blue and pink, multiplied. Yellow only as a ground or a highlight.
Fills slip 4px right and 3px down from the key. The slip is constant across a page.
Halftone dots at a 9px pitch, masked to a corner. No gradients.
Space Mono caps at 11px; the display face for the one big number.
Fractal-noise grain over covers and plates at 40% multiply.

motifs_note: The devices are the print shop’s: a word printed three times, a tag that hangs off a fact, a figure framed as a proof. Each is drawn with the hand variables, so it ports.

dos: Three inks and a key; let them multiply where they cross.
Print one word per page three times, slipped by a hair.
Hang facts on tags and folios in mono caps.
Open chapters full-bleed in one ink with the number enormous.
donts: No gradients, no blur, no rounded corners.
No yellow text and no yellow lines.
No fourth ink; status colours live in callouts and tags only.
No more than one ticker and one overprint word per page.
binding_losses: The overprint (three plates with a slip), multiply blending, the halftone screen, the manila tag stock, the hard shadow and the turn have no contract slot. They are carried as --ds-* properties and the ri-* classes above; kit components take paper, key, blue and yellow but stay square and flat.
footer: Paper first, Ink page second. Fonts: Fraunces 500/900 (SOFT 100, WONK 1) + 500 italic, Space Mono 400/700, Google-hosted.

tpl.slide_sub: Where a winter of broken bikes went, one ink per door.
tpl.slide_body: Of every 100 bikes through the depot door, this many rode out again. The rest became parts or scrap.
tpl.ed_deck: A winter of broken bikes, one depot, three doors. What came back, what became parts, and what was simply done.
tpl.ed_byline: Words and pictures: the depot · fictional batch · figures illustrative
tpl.ed_body: On a Monday in November a truck backs into the depot with five hundred bikes gathered from the docks. Each one gets a tag, a number and ten minutes of attention. By spring three hundred and ten of them are back on the street, a hundred and twenty-five have given their wheels and brakes to others, and sixty-five have gone to the recycler as clean steel.
steps: Five hundred bikes on the floor.
Each square is one bike; the ink is the door it will leave by. Nothing is decided yet.
Blue goes back to the docks, pink to the parts drawers, the pale ones to the recycler.
tpl.step_caption: Fig. 1 · One batch by door · illustrative
tpl.landing_headline: Every bike gets a second life.
tpl.landing_sub: Drop it at any dock. We tag it, fix it or part it out, and tell you which door it left by.
features: Most bikes need twenty minutes and one part. They go straight back out.
A cracked frame still has good wheels. They go to the drawers.
Clean steel to the recycler, weighed and counted.
